full_judgment:
5. The trial Court on consideration of the materials on record relating to 'Ka' schedule land i.e. plaintiffs' case of purchasing the land of said schedule by plaintiff No. 2 and the case of the contesting defendants as to purchasing the 'Ka' schedule by Izzatullah Chowdhury in the benami of plaintiff No.2 held that plaintiff No.2 is the real owner of the land in 'Ka' schedule. The trial Court while considering the case of the plaintiffs and the defendants as regard the land of' Kha' and 'Ga' schedule observed that question of possession of the property will not be of very much help to ascertain the real title of the land of 'Kha' and 'Ga' schedule. In the background of the admitted circumstances that Tofazzal Hossain till his death in 1353 BS with his wife Khatemon lived in the house of Izzatullah Chowdhury and after death of Tofazzal his wife Khatemon lived in the house of Izzatullah Chowdhury with children and, as such, "it is very difficult to distinguish the possession of Khatemon from that of Izzatullah Chowdhury", that question of inadequate consideration will not be a sufficient ground for taking the view that the transaction was a benami transfer since the transfer in question by Exhibit-l was made by a foster father in favour of his foster son, that passing of consideration as deposed by the scribe of Exhibit-1 in the proceeding under section 145 CrPC being of a professional deed writer in the absence of other independent witness cannot be relied upon safely and, as such, the matter or passing of consideration "does not help us much in determining the real dispute as to title", that the question of custody of the original document with plaintiff No.2 "does not help me very much in determining the real title" since from the evidence on record it is seen that PW 2's position in the house of Izzatullah Chowdhury "was that of a mistress" so long she was there and in that state of the matter it is quite probable that she took Exhibit-l in her custody and for which trouble started between her and lzzatullah Chowdhury and finally, she was driven out with her children from the house of Izzatullah Chowdhury, that the motive for making benami transaction by Exhibit-1 could not be established since lzzatullah Chowdhury "had no substantial debt to justify a Benami transaction for fear of any Marwari creditor", that in the background of dealing with the property of Exhibit-l i.e. property of khatian Nos. 28 and 47, by Izzatullah Chowdhury by the Exhibit- A dated 13-1-1944 and dealing with the property that Tofazzal's sister Amena Khatun got from lzzatullah Chowdhury by Exhibit-A and dealing with the said property as reflected by Exhibit-A(1) and Exhibit-A(2) clearly indicates that IzzatuJlah Chowdhury "did never intend to make any bonafide transfer by the earlier kabala Exhibitl in favour of his foster son Tofazzal Hossain", that the subsequent transfers by the kabalas Exhibits A(1) and A (2) are bonafide trans- fers, that Izzatullah Chowdhury transferred the land of khatian Nos. 28 and 47 by Exhibit-A to Tofazzal's sister Amena to his knowledge and that transfer made by Izzatullah Chowdhury to Tofazzal's sister Amena was a bonafide transfer, that from the rent decree Exhibit- 3(b) it cannot be said that the said rent suit was in respect of the land of khatian No. 31, that there is gulf of difference between the rent decree (Exhibit- 3(b) and the transfer made by the kabala Exhibit-A, that the Exhibit-A reveals the con-duct of Izzatullah Chowdhury and Tofazzal Hossain who are parties to the kabala, Exhibit-l but the Exhibit-3 reveals the conduct of the heirs of Tofazzal Hossain after his death and that it is also not known what was the nature of the ex parte rent decree, that discrepancies in the body of the kabala and the schedule thereof (Exhibit-1) sufficiently indicates that lzzatullah Chowdhury "made no bonafide transfer by the kabala Exhibit-1 ", since a vendor always takes reasonable care as regard the land he transferred when the same is a real one, that Exhibit-B series dakhilas as regard the land of Sandalpur, the lands in dispute are in the name of Izzatullah Chowdhury and the same are "more dependable than the dakhilas produced by the plaintiffs in their names", that in the facts and circumstances of the case it can reasonably be held that Izzatullah Chowdhury never intended to make "any bonafide and real transfer by the kabala Exhibit-1 in favour of his foster son Tofazzal Hossain." On the aforesaid findings and decisions the trial Court held that "neither Tofazzal nor the plaintiffs acquired any bonafide title in the disputed lands of Kha and Ga Schedule." As stated hereinbefore the trial Court decreed the suit in respect of the land of 'Ka' schedule but dismissed the suit in respect of the land of 'Kha' and 'Ga' schedule. 

 6. The plaintiffs as against the part of the judgment and decree of the trial Court i.e. dismissing the plaintiffs' suit in respect of the land of 'Kha' and 'Ga' schedule, went on appeal. From the defendants' side there was no appeal as against the judgment and decree of the trial Court decreeing the suit in respect of the land of Ka' schedule. The appellate Court set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court so far the same related to the land of 'Kha' and 'Ga' schedule on the findings that in the background of the materials on record, particularly evidence as to payment of consideration by Tofazzal Hossain in connection with Exhibit-1, the trial Court should have held that Exhibit-l is a valid document and the same was duly acted upon, that the trial Court, upon taking into consideration transaction made by Exhibit A, was in error in holding that Exhibit-I was not a bonafide deed of transfer and that it was not acted upon, that taking into consideration the fact that Exhibit-I was registered on 25th Falgoon, 1345 BS and Tofazzal Hossain married PW 2 in Baishakh, 1346 BS the contention of the plaintiffs that Exhibit- 1 was made for making provision for the future of TofazzaI cannot be lightly brushed aside, since in the background of the admitted position that Tofazzal Hossain and his wife, plaintiff No.2 stayed in the house of Izzatullah Chowdhury, that plaintiffs having had established by oral and documentary evidence that Tofazzal Hossain and after his death his heirs possessed the land of Exhibit-1 and the said fact clearly established the fact that by Exhibit-1 Tofazzal acquired title in the land of schedule 'Kha'' and 'Ga', that Exhibit-3(a), the certified copy of the rent decree, also shows that Tofazzal Hossain exercised his right and title in respect of the land of khatian No. 28 i.e. land of the 'Kha' schedule, that evidence of DW 2 proves the possession of the land in suit by the plaintiffs through bargader, that plaintiffs have succeeded in establishing that Tofazzal Hossain exclusively possessed the land of 'Kha' and 'Ga' schedule and the fact of possession of the land goes long way in determining the real nature of Exhibit-1, that because of the relationship between the vendor and vendee low price, as in the case of Exhibit-I cannot be the ground for holding that the transaction was a benami one, that payment of consideration money as regard the transaction made by the Exhibit-I has been proved by Exhibit- 8, the deposition of the scribe, that the trial Court was not well founded to discard the evidence of the scribe on the view that evidence of the scribe of Exhibit-I was of a professional deed writer since "deed writers under all circumstances do not depose falsely", that contention of the defendants that plaintiff No. 2 for illegal gain took away the Exhibit-l is nothing but a device "to nullify the effect of evidentiary value regarding custody of original document", that from the evidence of DWs it is seen that Izzatullah Chowdhury had no substantial debt upon borrowing from Marwari and, as such, the contention of the defendants that to put away the property or Exhibit-1 from the clutch of the creditor Izzatullah Chowdhury made Exhibit-1 is of no merit, that taking into consideration the fact of payment of consideration money by Tofazzal for the transaction evidenced by Exhibit-1 and possession of the land of Exhibit-1 by Tofazzal Hossain and after him his heirs and payment of rent to the Zamindar as well as to the Government by Tofazzal Hossain and his heirs and failure on the part of the defendants to prove that Exhibit-1 is a benami document, the only conclusion is that "kabala (Exhibit-1) is a bonafide, valid and active document. In fact, it operated to pass title in favour of Tofazzal," that presence of Tofazzal Hossain in the office of sub-Registrar on the date when by Exhibit-A, Izzatullah Chowdhury transferred 2.40½ acres of land of Exhibit-1 to. Tofazzal's sister, Arnena and by Exhibit-1 (a) Amena transferred land to her brother Tofazzal does not saddle Tofazzal Hossain with the knowledge of the transfer of land of Exhibit-1 by Izzatullah Chowdhury by the Exhibit-A to Amena, sister of Tofazzal Hossain, that the transaction made by Izzatullah Chowdhury by Exhibit-A and the transaction made by Amena by Exhibit-A(1) did not affect the validity of Exhibit-1 since the same has been found "a valid and bonafide document and title of the disputed land passed by it", that Exhibit-A executed by Izzatullah Chowdhury as regard the land of khatian Nos. 28 and 47 i.e. land of 'Kha' and 'Ga' schedule, "cannot nullify the effect of Exhibit-1 ", that there is nothing on the record to show what prompted Izzatullah Chowdhury to make sham transaction by Exhibit-1 , that when motive for making benami transaction by Exhibit-1 could not be proved by the defendants and it having been established that Izzatullah Chowdhury for the future provision of Tofazzal Hossain made Exhibit-1, as such "it can be reasonably presumed that transaction witnessed by Exhibit-1 is a bonafide and real one", that the conclusion so made gets supported from the subsequent transfer made by Izzatullah Chowdhury to plaintiff No. 2's son, plaintiff No. 4 by Exhibit-4, that in the context of the fact on record it cannot be said that Exhibit-I was not acted upon, that in the background of the consideration of the facts and the circumstance, only conclusion that can be derived is Exhibit-1" is a valid and active document and Tofazzal acquired valid title to the land of schedule Kha and Ga by virtue of that deed" and, as such, plaintiffs have right, title and possession in the land of 'Kha' and 'Ga' schedule. 

 14. It may be mentioned at no stage of the suit or the appeals i.e. appeal before the lower appellate Court and the High Court Division it was never the case of the plaintiffs that transaction by Exhibit-A by Izzatullah Chowdhury was an attempt on his part to defraud Tofazzal Hossain. No material was brought on record that at the relevant time i.e. on January 13, 1944 there was any occasion on the part Of Izzatullah Chowdhury to defraud his foster son by making transfer by Exhibit-A in favour of Tofazzal's sister. lzzatullah Chowdhury by Exhibit- A transferred 1.31 acres of land from khatian No. 28 and 1.9'/2 acres from khatian No. 47. No evidence has also been brought on record that relation between Izzatullah Chowdhury and his foster son had for any reason become sour or there had been misunderstanding or that there had been any incident whereby Tofazzal Hossain incurred displeasure of his foster father Izzatullah Chowdhury and that prompted lzzatullah Chowdhury to defraud Tofazzal Hossain by making transaction by the Exhibit-A. In that view of the matter we do not find any substance in the submission of the learned Counsel for the plaintiff respondents that transaction by Exhibit-A by lzzatullah Chowdhury was an attempt to defraud Tofazzal Hossain. The other submission was that transfer made by lzzatullah Chowdhury by Exhibit- A was hit by the provision of section 53 of the Act. The said submission is also of no merit since no situation as contemplates by the provision of section 53 of the Act was present in respect of the transfer made by Izzatullah Chowdhury by the Exhibit-A in favour of Amena, the sister of Tofazzal Hossain. 

 15. It may also be mentioned no such case was pleaded from the side of the plaintiffs at any point of time except in the course of hearing of the present appeal. It may be mentioned that on the day transaction by Exhibit-A was made by lzzatullah Chowdhury his foster son Tofazzal Hossain was very much present in the office of the Sub-Registrar. The lower appellate Court has observed that because of presence of Izzatullah Chowdhury on the date Exhibit-A was registered he cannot be fastened with the knowledge of transfer of the land of khatian Nos. 28 and 47 to his sister Amena by Exthibit A. In our opinion, the view so taken by the lower appellate Court appears to be not correct if considered in the context of normal course of business, in that there is no material on record to show that Tofazzal Hossain was in the office of the Sub-Registrar for some other business and that his presence in the office of the Sub-Registrar on the date in question i.e. when transfer was made by Exhibit-A, was a coincidence since he had been in the office of Sub-Registrar for some other business other than the business that was transacted by Izzatullah Chowdhury by Exhibit-A. It may be mentioned Exhibit-I was executed and registered on March 9, 1939 and the Exhibit-A was registered on January 13, 1944. So it is seen that the transfer by Exhibit-A was made by lzzatullah Chowdhury about 5 years after the Exhibit-1. As stated hereinbefore no material was brought on record to establish the contention that by Exhibit-A Izzatullah Chowdhury tried to defraud Tofazzal Hossain. It may be mentioned lower appellate Court as well as the High Court Division while arriving at the finding that transfer by Exhibit-I was not a benami transaction took into consideration the motive, custody of the document, possession of the land as in Exhibit-1 and payment of rent to the Zamindar and the Government.
